about: Removal roadmap for every entry of docs/planning/aivm-secrets-assumptions.json. tests/test_assumption_roadmap.py keeps the two files in sync: no assumption may exist without a class, justification, track, removal approach and priority. Classes: specification (operator/provider intent, mitigated by review), external-trusted (libraries/OS/toolchain, shrink and pin, never extracted), deployment (validated by host/VM evidence), open-obligation (tracked design gaps), python-reference (Python reference implementation only), native-trusted (project-owned native Rust, removable by further extraction).

entries.justification: serde_json is an external parser. Deferred by maintainer decision (2026-10-22): read confinement holds for every parsed document (read_confinement_for_every_document) and noninterference holds for any deterministic parse, so exact serde parity buys no confinement and only fixes which documents are compared. Exact parity (f64 overflow boundary, GraphQL zero test) is costly.
entries.removal: Optional later: an Aeneas-extracted provider body parser with a serde oracle; only if a reviewer needs the document to be a proved function of bytes.

entries.justification: Native reachability of credential bytes. Narrowed twice on 2026-10-22: the core owns channel construction/send/gate, and since then also the credential and its encoding during a request (native request primitives hold no credential). Aeneas cannot extract rustls/std/OS I/O or the custody/unsealing paths.
entries.removal: (1) DONE: native request primitives no longer receive the credential. (2) Make the credential a core-owned opaque type outside custody/unsealing. (3) Keep W3/W6 guards and mutation tests, including the no-credential-field pin. (4) Independent review of the remaining native call graph. Assessment 2026-10-24: Rust module privacy already confines the native Credential to custody. A core opaque type would retype every extracted function that takes the secret (and their proofs) while the remaining raw-byte readers (envelope seal, OAuth marker check, legacy account writer, inner-issue export) stay native; recommend a maintainer decision before doing step (2).

entries.justification: A handful of reviewed native lines connect native values to extracted functions.
entries.removal: Move each remaining call site into an extracted wrapper where Aeneas supports it (as done for channel_work and selected_release); keep guards for the rest. Assessment 2026-10-24: the remaining sites are enum/type conversions at the native-core boundary (e.g. status_error, GuestFrame::from_answer). Moving one into the core needs a native inverse map, so it relocates the glue without removing it; keep them pinned by the W3/NR-2/3 guards unless the core gains the native error type. Done 2026-10-24: the native Error is the extracted PublicError (its host spelling is PublicError::name, extracted), so the 17-arm native mapping is gone. The approval-decision line was removed 2026-10-24 (write_gate::run_admitted). Also done 2026-10-24: the Denial, UseDenial and StatusDenial maps are the extracted public_error::of_release/of_use/of_status.

entries.justification: Per-request sequencing is the extracted proxy_controller::serve (proved for any callbacks); what remains native is the Upstream callbacks, the CONNECT/tunnel loop and socket/TLS writes, with a reviewed write shape.
entries.removal: Done 2026-10-23: per-request controller (serve, with acknowledged admission and completion audits), CONNECT decision (admit) and head reader (connect_head), framing decision (frame), tunnel loop (tunnel/step) and the guest-side translator's sequencing (serve_translated) are extracted and proved. Remaining: byte-exact contracts for the native socket/TLS reads and writes, the audit file append, the bridge client call and the session clock, as for the bridge writer.

Remaining: represent ControlState revocation as the same current-admission state the request path checks.
